subject: Dedicated reservation options and step-up schedule — Kestrel Bio
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@kestrelbio.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and step-up schedule — Kestrel Bio

Samir,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — great to learn more about the Kestrel annotation pipelines and your Q4/2027 latency targets. Per our discussion, attached is a concise options worksheet with three reservation structures we recommend depending on your desired tradeoff between unit cost and operational headroom. High-level summary below, with the worksheet attached (Kestrel_Reserve_Options_v1.xlsx).

Option A — Conservative baseline (lower capex commitment)- Cluster: 8x A100 80GB GPUs (single region, us-west-2)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 4- Ramp schedule: Month 0-1: 25% activation (warm-start cached images)
  Month 2-3: 60% activation
  Month 4: 100% active- Burst allowance: up to +30% burstable via shared pool, subject to availability- Best if you want minimal upfront spend and faster ability to decommit

Option B — Balanced (recommended for production ML workloads)- Cluster: 16x A100 80GB GPUs (primary with hot-standby replicas across AZs)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8- Ramp schedule: Month 0: 40% active (initial onboarding)
  Month 1-2: 75% active (model optimization window)
  Month 3: 100% active (SLA go-live)- Burst allowance: +50% with pre-warmed instances for predictable latency- Includes model warm-start credit for first 60 days to reduce token cost during tuning

Option C — Aggressive runway (best long-term unit economics)- Cluster: 32x A100 80GB GPUs (multi-region: us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 warm standby)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 16- Ramp schedule: Month 0: 60% active
  Month 1: 100% active (staged canary rollout)- Burst allowance: +80% with guaranteed corridor for urgent jobs (SLA-dependent)- Pricing assumes 12–24 month commit for deepest discount

Key operational notes (high level):
- Warm-start credits: first 60 days for model compilation/kv cache seeding (applies to B and C)
- Canary windows: we recommend canary lanes in weeks 5–8 for B/C to validate scale and latency SLOs
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to a quantized variant of the model if live latency exceeds target for >3m
- Prewarming: we can reserve prewarmed instances for scheduled large-batch jobs (pricing on worksheet)

Ask: please indicate which option aligns best with your procurement runway (preferred commit length) and any hard constraints (max spend / earliest go-live / regional requirements). We can then convert the worksheet into a contract-ready proposal + SOW.

Next steps I propose:
- You pick A/B/C (or request a custom combo)
- We produce a finalized proposal with exact pricing and activation milestones
- Kickoff & onboarding call (30–45m) within one week of signed PO

Attaching: Kestrel_Reserve_Options_v1.xlsx (contains cost, activation calendar, and sample SLA language).

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: Kestrel_Reserve_Options_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with SKU-level pricing and activation timeline)

From: Samir Khan <samir@kestrelbio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and step-up schedule — Kestrel Bio

Ben —

Thanks for the clear options. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement:

1) Burst guarantees: for Option B, you mention +50% burst with pre-warmed instances — is that a hard SLA or best-effort? We need predictability for high-priority inference during peak batch windows.
2) Warm-start credits: can you confirm what "60 days" covers (is it compile time only or also token credits while finetuning)?
3) If we choose Option C with multi-region, what's the minimum notice for activating the secondary region (and is there any extra warm-up cost)?
4) Pricing cadence: curious how much better 24-month looks vs 12-month for Option C (rough % range is fine).

Goal: get a version we can hand to procurement that calls out activation milestones and acceptance criteria. Also please confirm whether we can include a one-time onboarding milestone tied to a fixed set of deliverables (e.g., 5 validated prompt sets, latency reports, handover checklist).

Samir
VP Engineering, Kestrel Bio
samir@kestrelbio.com

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samir,
>
> Thanks again for the call yesterday — great to learn more about the Kestrel annotation pipelines and your Q4/2027 latency targets. Per our discussion, attached is a concise options worksheet with three reservation structures we recommend depending on your desired tradeoff between unit cost and operational headroom...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@kestrelbio.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and step-up schedule — Kestrel Bio

Samir — thanks for the great questions, adding technical detail here so procurement has line items they can rely on. Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through the worksheet row-by-row.

1) Burst guarantees (Option B):
- The +50% burst is a contractual corridor we can reserve behind a higher-price burst SKU. For guaranteed low-latency during peak windows we recommend combining: (a) pre-warmed burst instances (reserved and billed at a lower discount tier than the main fleet), and (b) a scheduled pre-scaling window tied to expected batch runs. If you require hard guaranteed capacity during arbitrary unscheduled peaks, we can add an SLA clause with a dedicated hot-standby lane (cost: ~20–30% premium on top of Option B base).

2) Warm-start credits scope:
- 60 days covers server-side compilation and KV-cache seeding plus a capped token-credit pool for interactive tuning (up to 10M tokens). Heavy continuous finetuning beyond that is billed separately — we can include a capped retainer if you expect extended tuning.

3) Multi-region activation (Option C):
- Secondary region (us-east-1) activation notice: typically 14 days for full warm-up into a production-ready state if you want KV caches pre-seeded and binaries compiled. If you accept a soft-warmup (no KV seeds) we can bring capacity in ~72 hours, but latency for cold requests will be higher initially. Extra warm-up cost for pre-seeding is equivalent to ~3 days of reserved GPU billing for the size of the secondary cluster (line item in worksheet).

4) Pricing cadence: 12 vs 24 months (Option C)- 24-month commit: additional ~12–18% discount over 12-month pricing (depends on exact cluster size and GPU model). We can firm the final range in the proposal appendix.

Additional: onboarding milestone proposal (agreed deliverables) — yes, we can define a one-time onboarding milestone with the following acceptance criteria: 5 validated prompt sets with end-to-end latency < target, model artifacts and versioning in your repo, and a handover doc + runbook. We can attach that as SOW Exhibit A.

I'll annotate the worksheet with these line items and send an updated file this afternoon.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
